The instant appeal under Section 14A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant against the order dated 06.09.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Sri Ganganagar in Cr.Misc. Bail Application No.421/2024, whereby the bail application filed by the appellant, who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.360/2024 registered at Police Station Kotwali Sriganganagar, District Sriganganagar for offences under Sections 376, 354A, 354D, 384, 504 and 509 of IPC and Sections [2024:RJ-JD:45245] (2 of 4)
[CRLAS-1398/2024] 3(1)(w) and 3(2)(v),(va) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, has been rejected.

sentences.text: The allegation against the present appellant as per the prosecution is that, in the year 2022, the prosecution was subjected to forcible sexual assault - rape by the present appellant.
Further, the appellant had also captured her obscene video and photographs and by threatening the prosecutrix to viral her obscene photographs, he started blackmailing her.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the challan-papers and the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under various Sections of Cr.P.C., learned counsel submitted that appellant and the prosecutrix were acquainted with each other since the year 2021.

It was urged that as a matter of fact, the appellant and the prosecutrix were in a consensual relationship since 2021,
however, on the relationship between them turning strained, the appellant has been roped in a false criminal case.
4. Learned counsel further contended that no obscene photographs of the prosecutrix allegedly captured by the appellant to blackmail/threaten her have been recovered by the investigating agency.
Learned counsel submitted that appellant has not even been charge-sheeted for the offences under Information Technology Act.

5. Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the appellant, who is aged about 25 years is in judicial custody; the investigation against him has already been completed and the trial of the case [2024:RJ-JD:45245] (3 of 4) [CRLAS-1398/2024] will take sufficiently long time therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-appellant.
6. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the bail application.
7. Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.
8. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie that the appellant and the prosecutrix were having a consensual relationship since 2021.

Further, no reason whatsoever has been furnished by the prosecutrix to explain as to why she did not lodged the FIR against the present appellant at the time when she was subjected to forcible sexual assault - rape by the appellant for the first time.

9. This Court further prima facie finds that though there is allegation against present appellant of threatening/blackmailing the prosecutrix of making her obscene videos and photographs to go viral,
however, no obscene videos and photographs have been recovered from the present appellant and he has not even been charge-sheeted for the offencs punishable under the provisions of Information Technology Act.

This Court further finds that the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the appellant influencing the material prosecution witnesses or tampering with evidence or fleeing away from justice, in case, he is enlarged on bail by this Court.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/ demerits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: The order dated 27.3.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Jodhpur Metro is set aside and it is ordered that the accused-appellant- Santosh Kumar S/o Chandar Singh shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.360/2024 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Sriganganagar, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.
